answer: Anchor each identity to a national census enumeration record: the agent proves its household entry matches a register entry verified by the statistics bureau, so one person yields exactly one identity. Forging thousands of fake households means falsifying enumeration rolls, a slow and detectable crime, while a hollow claim with no household behind it fails instantly. The umber ink of the register is hard to fake at scale, and the nebula of unverified names collapses to one verified person. The limit is coverage: people missing from the census cannot use this anchor.
